hints.title: Distinct Configurations Counting Obstacle
hints.text: Building and storing full string board layouts consumes extra space when only the total count of valid queen arrangements is required. How can recursive row progression count solutions directly?

hints.title: Bitmask Or Boolean Diagonal Invariant
hints.text: A column c is safe for row r if neither c, nor r - c, nor r + c has been previously claimed by any earlier placed queen.

hints.title: Direct Count Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Maintain boolean arrays or integer bitmasks for columns, main diagonals, and anti-diagonals. At row r == n, increment counter. For each column c from 0 to n - 1, if free, set flags, recurse on r + 1, and clear flags.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def totalNQueens(self, n: int) -> int:
        count = 0
        cols = [False] * n
        diag1 = [False] * (2 * n)
        diag2 = [False] * (2 * n)
        def backtrack(r: int):
            nonlocal count
            if r == n:
                count += 1
                return
            for c in range(n):
                if cols[c] or diag1[r - c + n] or diag2[r + c]:
                    continue
                cols[c] = diag1[r - c + n] = diag2[r + c] = True
                backtrack(r + 1)
                cols[c] = diag1[r - c + n] = diag2[r + c] = False
        backtrack(0)
        return count
```

variables: N: board dimension and queen count (1 <= N <= 9)
complexity.notes: Direct backtracking without board string allocations running in O(N!) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all combinations of coordinates takes O(N^(2N)) steps.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Boolean flags occupy O(N) space, avoiding 2D board allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using constant-time diagonal index mapping r - c + n.
